name: mxgemmini_rtl_dim32
description: DIM=32 variant of mxgemmini_rtl.json (MxDim32E4M3VpuGemminiRocketConfig, E4M3 single on a 32x32 mesh): 32-deep PE column (window 32), lanes 0-14 the dim16 ramp and lanes 15-31 bf16 (dim32MxFPConfig meshAccPrecisionList: gemmini.cc acc_e/acc_m, 'lanes 0-15 = the dim16 ramp; lanes 16+ = bf16'), same product format. Not yet checked against RTL: graded against spike libgemmini_dim32.so.

mesh.comment: window is the 16-deep PE column; block is the E8M0 group. Both must match or the lane indexing shifts.

formats.comment: The operand scale convention is MXQuant's own end-to-end convention, which the FP8 datapath was migrated to. Operands need NO change -- they already match bit-for-bit.

acc_schedule_source: gemmini.cc mx_loop_ws_spad (GEMMINI_DIM > 8): kk < 8 -> (4,4), kk < 10 -> (4,5), kk < 15 -> (4,6), else (8,7). Entries are [exp_bits, man_bits] per lane, lane = k % window.

product_quantize.detail: Mantissa TRUNCATION to man bits, with NO exponent clamp and no subnormal grid at the product stage. NOT float_quantize(rounding='nearest').
product_quantize.source: fp8_matmul_model.mx_product_quantize_trunc; MxFPMul.scala product path before the accumulator resize

accumulate.detail: Quantize BOTH the running sum and the incoming product to the lane's (exp, man) with round-to-nearest-even, then add exactly: C = fp_add_exact(fp_quantize_rne(C, e, m), fp_quantize_rne(outer, e, m), e, m). The product is therefore quantized TWICE -- once to e4m3, again to the accumulator lane.
accumulate.mxquant_as_shipped: S_red = S_red + outer_q (fp32); S_red = float_quantize(S_red, e, m, 'nearest')  -- only the SUM is quantized  (eval_complete.py:608-614)

cross_tile_accumulate.detail: Each 16-deep tile result is scaled, rounded to bf16, and accumulated in bf16: C = bf16_accum_add(C, q_bf16_rne(S_red * scale_map)).
cross_tile_accumulate.source: fp8_matmul_model.py:718-724; gemmini.cc:1190 (mx_smem is bf16 and accumulates)

important: These three do NOT decompose. Applied singly, each one LOWERS the error versus fp32 (10.63% -> 9.03% or 8.65%) and two of the three make the divergence from the hardware WORSE (17.90% -> 8.83% / 12.55%). Only all three together are bit-exact. Do not quote the effect of one of them measured with the other two unmatched.

primitives_from.comment: Relative to this directory (npu-exploration/rtl_exact). The exact-dyadic primitives (mx_product_quantize_trunc, fp_quantize_rne, fp_add_exact, q_bf16_rne, bf16_accum_add) are IMPORTED from the hardware golden model rather than transcribed here, so there is one implementation and it cannot drift. rtl_datapath.py fails loudly if the path is wrong instead of falling back to a lookalike.
